claim: Native Bakairi syllable codas are restricted to glides; ordinary native consonants do not occupy coda position.

source_forms.generalization: only glides are allowed in coda position
source_forms.qualification: ideophones can show exceptional glottal-stop codas/CVC shapes

normalized_environment: CODA -> G in ordinary native vocabulary
scope: native vocabulary described in phonology chapter
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Ideophones are treated separately and may contain a glottal stop in coda position, so the restriction is not generalized to that marginal class.

claim: Several consonant-vowel combinations are unattested in the described lexicon, while /te/ is explicitly rare rather than absent.

source_forms.rare: te occurs in only three words in the described corpus

normalized_environment: lexical CV cooccurrence gaps; /te/ low frequency
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The author presents these as unattested combinations in the corpus, not as a proof of absolute phonological impossibility; /te/ is attested three times.

claim: Word-initial nonsonorant stops surface voiceless, neutralizing the voicing contrast at the left edge; the corresponding root-initial consonants can surface voiced when a vowel-final prefix places them word-medially.
normalized_environment: nonsonorant -> [-voice] / #__; voiced realization available word-medially after prefixation
scope: native lexical items and prefixed forms
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Ideophones and the ethnonym/name Bakairi are discussed as exceptions/marginal material; the latter is likely a loan. Recent Portuguese loans may also retain initial voicing.

claim: In polysyllabic native words, at most one non-initial obstruent is normally voiceless; the position of that voiceless consonant is lexically unpredictable and other eligible consonants are voiced by default.

source_forms.generalization: only one non-initial voiceless consonant in a polysyllabic word

normalized_environment: native polysyllabic word normally permits <=1 noninitial [-voice] obstruent
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The grammar explicitly lists several lexical exceptions and one free-variation pair, so this is a strong generalization rather than an exceptionless ban.

claim: /s/ has a restricted word-internal distribution: only one internal occurrence is normally found, it combines there with non-close vowels /e a ə o/, and it is realized [ʃ] before the close vowels /i, ĩ, u/.
normalized_environment: s -> ʃ / __ {i,ĩ,u}; internal /s/ distribution restricted by vowel quality and count
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The record preserves the grammar's distributional description; loanword phonotactics may differ.

claim: /h/ is word-medial and does not form syllables with the front vowels /i, e, ĩ/ in the native distribution described; it also occurs as the onset of suffixal syllables containing back vowels /u, o/.
normalized_environment: native hV excludes front {i,e,ĩ}; h is not ordinary word-initial consonant
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Marginal or borrowed patterns are not promoted to native phonotactic status.

claim: The rhotic and lateral are syllable-initial but only rarely word-initial; the grammar additionally reports a dialectal skew, with /r/ especially prominent medially in Eastern Bakairi and sparse in the Western variety.

source_forms.dialect: medial /r/ markedly more prominent in Eastern than Western Bakairi

normalized_environment: liquids favor non-word-initial onset position; /r/ frequency dialect-conditioned
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Word-initial liquids are rare, not categorically excluded.

claim: The basic Bakairi syllable is (C)V with a vowel nucleus and optional onset; apparent complex sequences involving glides yield the attested surface templates V, CV, GV, VG, CGV and CVG, but are not analyzed as ordinary consonant clusters.

source_forms.analysis: glides account for apparent complex margins; no true CC clusters

normalized_environment: σ = (C)V with glide-bearing extensions; no ordinary CC
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Ideophones constitute a marginal class with additional shapes, including glottal codas.

claim: Most Bakairi words contain at least two syllables, and a monosyllabic word must contain a long vowel, yielding a bimoraic minimal-word requirement.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The grammar allows monosyllables when they satisfy bimoraicity; it does not impose categorical disyllabicity.

claim: In CGV sequences whose consonant is /s/ or /h/, the glide can variably delete and the fricative realization alternates accordingly; the same speaker may produce both variants.

source_forms.process: variable glide deletion with concomitant fricative alternation

normalized_environment: G -> Ø variably / {s,h} __ V, with fricative allophony
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The process is variable rather than obligatory, and the grammar specifically identifies /s,h/ contexts rather than all CGV sequences.
